title: Rav Avya Saba of Pumbedita
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: At the opening of his argument, Hyman places him among the leading sages of the generation in Rav Huna’s time, as in Beitzah 21a, where he asked Rav Huna, and Rav Huna said to him, “A raven flew” (he diverted him to another matter — Rashi). When he went out, Rabbah his son said to him: “Is this not Rav Avya Saba, whom the Master praises, for he is a great man?” He said to him: “What could I do? Today I am supported by raisin-cakes, and he asked me something that requires reasoning.” In Chullin 124b it is cited that he asked Rabbah son of Rav Huna, and Rava his son asked him: “Is this not Rav Avya Saba of Pumbedita?” Hyman explains this as Yuchasin’s intent in the entry Rav Avya: “Rav Avya Saba, who is a great man; and likewise Rabbah son of Rav Huna to Rava his son” — he means the two Gemara passages: Beitzah 21a, where Rabbah said this of him to Rav Huna his father, and Chullin 124b, where it is Rabbah son of Rav Huna and Rava his son. And what Yuchasin cites under the entry Rava, “Rava son of Rav Avya Saba to Rav Ashi, as in Menachot,” undoubtedly was his reading; and this is not the son of the Rav Avya Saba who lived in Rav Huna’s time, as Hyman explains in his entry. Seder HaDorot needlessly criticized him under the entry Rava son of Rav Avya Saba and argued at length needlessly.

Hyman’s final position is that two errors have entered the Gemara passages: in Chullin he proposes the reading in Beitzah there, that he came before Rav Huna and not before Rabbah son of Rav Huna, as the reading is cited in Dikdukei Soferim on Chullin 124b; and likewise we find him with Rabbah son of Rav Huna, as in Pesachim 51a: “When Rabbah bar bar Chana came, Rav Avya Saba (so is the reading of the Rif; our Gemara has Avira Saba) and Rabbah son of Rav Huna went in to him … they came and told his father (that is, Rav Huna).” In both places Hyman proposes Rav Yeiva Saba and not Rav Avya Saba, for Rav Yeiva Saba was indeed one of Rav’s students, and this reading is cited in Dikdukei Soferim there. But Rav Avya Saba was much later, for he discussed matters with Rav Papa, as in Moed Katan 24b, “Rav Papa led Rav Avya Saba and he expounded,” and in Sanhedrin 57b he raised a difficulty against Rav Papa. Hyman regards this as clear.

notes.text: Both stages of Hyman’s argument are retained, including the initial Avya-in-Huna’s-time hypothesis and final preference for Yeiva in those passages and a much later Avya. Yuchasin’s citations and SederHaDorot criticism remain attributed; the phrasing argued at length needlessly avoids inventing a personal attack by an earlier author against Hyman. The raisin-cakes phrase stays the supplied Scriptural allusion.

The consulted Beitzah 21a has Avya asking Huna and Rabbah addressing his father; Chullin 124b instead has Avya asking Rabbah bar Huna and Rava his son responding. Pesachim 51a reads Avira Saba and says they told Abaye, whereas Hyman reports the Rif’s Avya and identifies the recipient as Huna his father. These consulted differences are disclosed without rewriting the supplied body or current note. Hyman’s initial hypothesis and final clear Yeiva reconstruction both remain intact.
